lessons.title: Listen and speak: describing people at work
lessons.objective: Describe a person and what he or she does in simple sentences.
lessons.course:
We describe people with simple words: She is tall. He is old. She has a basket.
We say their work: He is a farmer. She is a nurse. He is a tailor. She is a teacher.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
He is a farmer.
She is a nurse.
He has a hoe.

lessons.model: The adult shows a drawing: “This is Mr Mbah. He is a farmer. He is tall. He has a hoe.”
lessons.guided: Look at drawings of workers. For each one, say two sentences: what the person is, what he or she has.
lessons.exercise: Describe a farmer in one sentence.
lessons.answer: For example: He is a farmer. He has a hoe.
lessons.remediation: Use only “He is a …” or “She is a …” with three pictures.
lessons.transfer: Describe the work of one adult in your family.
lessons.materials: Drawings of workers (farmer, nurse, tailor, teacher, driver).

practice.prompt: Match each worker with a tool.
practice.answer: farmer: hoe; tailor: needle; teacher: chalk.
practice.explanation: Each worker uses tools.

practice.prompt: Listen and say after the voice.
practice.listen: She is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
practice.answer: She is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
practice.explanation: Say the whole sentence.

practice.prompt: Who works in a hospital?
practice.explanation: Nurses care for sick people in a hospital.

lessons.title: Read: sh and ch
lessons.objective: Read the digraphs sh and ch and words containing them.
lessons.course:
Two letters can make one sound. s and h together make sh, like when we ask for silence: shhh. c and h together make ch, like a train: ch, ch, ch.
Words: shop, fish, ship, chin, chop, rich.

support.title: Read with the adult
support.text:
sh: shop  fish  ship
ch: chin  chop  chip

lessons.model: The adult reads: “sh-o-p: shop. The tailor has a shop.” Then: “ch-o-p: chop. The cook chops onions.”
lessons.guided: Sort word cards into two groups: words with sh and words with ch. Read each word aloud.
lessons.exercise: Read the word: f – i – sh.
lessons.remediation: Say the sound sh several times with a finger on the lips, then read sh + one more sound.
lessons.transfer: Find a word with sh or ch on a shop sign or a box.
lessons.materials: Word cards with sh and ch.

practice.prompt: Which word has the sound sh?
practice.explanation: s and h make sh in ship.

practice.prompt: Complete with sh or ch.
practice.text: The fisherman sells fi[[sh]]. The cook [[ch]]ops onions.
practice.explanation: fish ends with sh; chop starts with ch.

practice.prompt: Put the sounds in order to make “shop”.
practice.explanation: sh is one sound made by two letters.

lessons.title: Write: letters n to z
lessons.objective: Form the small letters n to z from left to right, on the line.
lessons.course:
We finish the alphabet: n, o, p, q, r, s, t, u, v, w, x, y, z. The letters p, q and y go below the line. The letter t is a little tall.
Now we can write all the letters of the alphabet.

support.title: Trace with the adult
support.text:
n o p q r s t
u v w x y z

lessons.model: The adult writes p: “A stick down below the line, then round.” Then y: “A small v, then a tail below the line.”
lessons.guided: Trace each letter, then write it three times. Say its sound. Circle the letters that go below the line.
lessons.exercise: Write the letters p, q, y.
lessons.answer: p q y, with their tails below the line.
lessons.remediation: Practise the letters that go below the line with a coloured line under the writing line.
lessons.transfer: Write the name of a job: a tailor, a nurse.

practice.prompt: Write the letters r, s, t.
practice.answer: r s t, on the line.
practice.explanation: t is a little taller than r and s.

practice.prompt: Put the last letters of the alphabet in order.
practice.explanation: z is the last letter of the alphabet.

practice.prompt: Write the word “tailor”.
practice.explanation: t-a-i-l-o-r.

lessons.title: Action words: the simple present
lessons.objective: Use action verbs in the simple present with I, you, he and she.
lessons.course:
A verb is an action word: sell, cook, drive, sew.
With I, you, we and they, the verb does not change: I cook. They sell.
With he and she, we add s: He drives. She sews. The baker bakes bread.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
I cook. → She cooks.
I drive. → He drives.

lessons.model: The adult mimes and says: “I sew.” Then points to a picture: “The tailor sews.”
lessons.guided: Mime an action; the child says what you do with he or she and adds s.
lessons.remediation: Practise only with “she”: she cooks, she sells, she sings.
lessons.transfer: Say three things that people in your family do every day.

practice.prompt: Add the missing letter.
practice.text: She sell[[s]] fish. He cook[[s]] rice.
practice.answer: She sells fish. He cooks rice.
practice.explanation: With he and she, the verb takes s.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
practice.explanation: With he, add s: drives.

practice.prompt: Complete: The baker ___ (bake) bread.
practice.explanation: With the baker (he or she), add s.

lessons.title: Money: our coins up to 100 francs
lessons.objective: Recognise coins and pay small amounts up to 100 francs.
lessons.course:
We use coins of 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 francs.
Two coins of 50 francs make 100 francs. Two coins of 25 francs make 50 francs.
We count the coins to pay the right amount.
lessons.model: At the shop, a pencil costs 50 francs. The adult pays with two coins of 25 francs: “25 and 25 make 50.”
lessons.guided: Play shop with real or paper coins. Pay for small things in different ways.
lessons.exercise: A sweet costs 25 francs. You pay with 50 francs. How much change do you get?
lessons.remediation: Use only coins of 50 and 100 francs at first.
lessons.transfer: With an adult, look at the coins in a purse and say their values.
lessons.materials: Coins or paper coins of 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 francs.

practice.prompt: 50 francs + 50 francs = ? francs
practice.explanation: Two coins of 50 make 100 francs.

practice.prompt: Which coins make 30 francs?
Match each price with the coins.
practice.explanation: Add the coins.

lessons.title: Number bonds to 10
lessons.objective: Build the pairs of numbers that make 10 and use them to add quickly.
lessons.course:
Number bonds are pairs that make a number. The bonds of 10: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 3 + 7, 4 + 6, 5 + 5.
If I know 6 + 4 = 10, I know 4 + 6 = 10 too.
lessons.model: The adult shows ten fingers, folds 3: “3 folded, 7 standing. 3 and 7 make 10.”
lessons.guided: Use ten bottle tops in two hands. Move some from one hand to the other and say the bond each time.
lessons.remediation: Use ten fingers to see each bond.
lessons.transfer: Play with a friend: one says a number, the other says what makes 10.

practice.explanation: 6 and 4 make 10.

practice.prompt: Match the numbers that make 10.
practice.explanation: Each pair makes 10.

practice.prompt: Complete the bonds.
practice.explanation: Think: what is missing to make 10?

lessons.title: Adding up to 50
lessons.objective: Add numbers up to 50 using tens and units, and solve simple problems about work.
lessons.course: To add 23 + 14, we add the tens and the units: 2 tens + 1 ten = 3 tens; 3 units + 4 units = 7 units. 23 + 14 = 37.
lessons.model: A tailor sews 20 shirts on Monday and 15 on Tuesday. The adult adds: “20 + 15: 3 tens and 5 units: 35 shirts.”
lessons.guided: Make each number with bundles and sticks, put them together, then count the tens and the units.
lessons.exercise: A farmer picks 21 cocoa pods, then 12 more. How many pods?
lessons.remediation: Add a number of tens first (20 + 10), then add numbers with units.
lessons.transfer: Make up a problem about a job you know and solve it.
lessons.materials: Bundles of ten sticks, loose sticks.

practice.explanation: 3 tens + 1 ten = 4 tens; 2 + 5 = 7 units: 47.

practice.prompt: A carpenter makes 10 chairs and then 20 chairs. How many chairs?
Complete.
practice.explanation: Add tens with tens, units with units.

lessons.title: Straight lines and curved lines
lessons.objective: Recognise and draw straight lines and curved lines, and make shapes and letters with them.
lessons.course:
A straight line does not bend, like the edge of a ruler. A curved line bends, like a rainbow.
Shapes and letters are made of lines: a triangle has three straight lines; the letter C is a curve.
lessons.model: The adult shows the tools of workers: “The ruler of the carpenter is straight. The rim of the basin is curved.”
lessons.guided: With a string, make a straight line, then a curved line. Draw both in sand, then on paper.
lessons.exercise: Is the letter O made of straight lines or curved lines?
lessons.remediation: Trace straight and curved lines on a model before drawing them alone.
lessons.transfer: Find three straight lines and three curved lines in your house.

practice.prompt: Which letter has only straight lines?
practice.explanation: L is made of two straight lines.

practice.prompt: Draw a straight line and a curved line.
practice.answer: One straight line and one curved line.
practice.explanation: Use a ruler for the straight line.

practice.prompt: Match each thing with its kind of line.
practice.answer: ruler: straight; rainbow: curved; door edge: straight.
practice.explanation: A straight line does not bend.
